source: Tears of Steel (CC BY 3.0, (CC) Blender Foundation | mango.blender.org), 1920x800, 24 fps

crop.audio: none (silent; original soundtrack licence is no-derivatives)

shots.caption: He hasn't noticed yet.
shots.why: Hold while the caption is read (Thom's head drifts 760-825 px, stays inside 595-1045); from 283.0 follow his drift left so his face keeps looking room right and the robot enters the right edge; cut at 288.5 before the back of his head leaves the window; head trimmed 2 s so the robot arrives 5.5 s in.

shots.caption: It is right behind him.
shots.why: Hold on the robot face (eyes at about 810-1260 px); S1 only showed an edge of the robot, this cut gives the full face as new information.

shots.caption: Face to face.
shots.why: Hold at 600-1050 px: Thom whole (585-786 px) on the left, the robot fills the right 45% where he looks; the only frame that relates man and machine.

shots.caption: Later: the real conversation.
shots.why: Hold on Thom's face (465-900 px across the shot); Celia's head starts at 1200 px, so the over-the-shoulder cannot fit in 450 px - it becomes a clean single; caption marks the time jump.

shots.caption: "We have to follow our passions"
shots.why: The holographic line is 780 px wide and can never fit 450 px, so frame the houses and the text centre and let the source rack focus reveal it; our caption restores the full line below the hologram (hologram sits at 0.26-0.56).

shots.caption: He waits for her answer.
shots.why: The face is 690 px wide, wider than the crop; keep eyes, nose and mouth (645-1020 px) and lose the left ear/hair; held full length because it is the emotional peak and the face does the work.

shots.caption: She isn't convinced.
shots.why: Hold at 935-1385 px: full face (features 990-1320 px) with the small space on the left where she looks (toward Thom), right ear trimmed; eyeline matches S6 (he looks right, she looks left).

punch_in: none - every key is scale 1.0; the source has 0 px headroom (800 px tall = output height), so any scale > 1.0 upscales.
